hero.title: File:3rd Winchester 1 Infantry Beg.png
hero.artist: Theodore F. Lang is the source book's author. TwoScarsUp added the color highlights and minor additions.
hero.credit: This map is from the unnumbered page after page 334 of the book "Loyal West Virginia from 1861 to 1865" published in 1895. TwoScarsUp has added highlights of the Union and Confederate positions plus an arrow marking the Berryville Pike and labels for the Martinsburg and Valley Pikes. Wickham and Lee's positions have also been noted per the Library of Congress Map titled "Battle field of Winchester, Va. (Opequon) [September 19, 1864]".
hero.description: Union and Confederate positions prior to Union infantry attack in Third Battle of Winchester that occurred September 19, 1864. Confederate (red) units are divisions except Wickham, Lee, and Payne are brigades.The (blue) Union corps (and Crook) consist of two or three divisions each. Wilson is a cavalry division. Arrow points to important Berryville Pike and its "canyon".

gallery.title: File:William W. Averell.jpg
gallery.artist: Mathew Brady (died 1896)
gallery.credit: Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, Brady's National Photographic Portrait Galleries  The exact same photo was published near the front of History of the Third Pennsylvania Cavalry, Sixtieth Regiment Pennsylvania Volunteers, in the American Civil War, 1861-1865., Volume 3, Part 4, which was published by the Franklin Printing Company in Philadelphia in 1905. The author is listed as United States, 3rd Pennsylvania Calvary Regiment. The cover of the book says William Brooke Rawie, and the inside says "Compiled by the Regimental History Committee in Accordance with a Resolution of the Third Pennsylvania Cavalry Association." The OCLC number is 1683643.
gallery.description: William Woods Averell (1832–1900) was a United States Army officer and a cavalry general in the American Civil War. After the war he was a diplomat and became wealthy by inventing American asphalt pavement.

Map of battlefield core and study areas.
Also known as Third Battle of Winchester.

The revised Study Area was expanded to include Core Areas associated with the action at Berryville Canyon and the Federal cavalry attack on the Confederate left.

gallery.title: File:Union Plan Third Winchester.png
gallery.artist: Sifton, Praed & Company, Ltd. modified by TwoScarsUp
gallery.credit: This is a portion of a 1912 map created by Sifton, Praed & Co. that has been modified by TwoScarsUp.  The entire map can be found in the Library of Congress map, and shows Virginia and Maryland. Modifications are based on Sheridan's memoirs and Patchan's book "The Last Battle of Winchester: Phil Sheridan, Jubal Early, and the Shenandoah Valley Campaign, August 7-September 19, 1864".
gallery.description: This map outlines General Philip Sheridan's plan to attack Jubal Early's army at Winchester, Virginia during the American Civil War in September 1864.
